about: Dated cache of platform icon rules, read by brandkit.py icon-export. Every number was read on verified_on from the platform's own page (source_urls). A null or an entry under `unverified` is a value nobody read on an official page: never fill it from memory. When a store or tool rejects a file, the official page wins and this file is corrected.
unverified: Apple: no current page read on verified_on states the 'no alpha' rule for the App Store icon; the archived QA1686 (2016) allows an alpha channel without transparent regions. The iOS master is written opaque WITHOUT an alpha channel, which satisfies both readings.
Apple: corner radius, squircle formula and macOS artwork inset are not published on the pages read; `macos.radius` is this project's drawing choice, not Apple's grid.
Android: pixel sizes per density are arithmetic (108 dp x density factor); no page lists them. Legacy launcher PNGs (API 25 and lower) are not produced.
Chrome: the 192 px and 512 px install requirement was read on pages dated 2024; whether current Chrome still enforces it was not confirmed.
apple-touch-icon: 180x180 is the largest size in Apple's archived example (2016); no current Apple page states a required size.
SVG favicons: no first-party browser document was read; the HTML Standard defines `sizes="any"` for scalable icons. Google Search does not list SVG among its favicon formats.
ICO: PNG entries and the 0 = 256 convention come from Microsoft developer blog posts (2010) and a Windows 7-era guide, not from a formal specification.

ios.label: iOS, iPadOS and App Store master
notes: Layout 1024x1024 px, square; the system masks the corners: deliver unmasked artwork.
Xcode builds every iOS, iPadOS and watchOS size from one 1024x1024 image (the default behaviour).
The system generates dark, clear and tinted variants that are not provided.
Icon Composer layered icons are made in Apple's tool from the SVG mark; this export does not write that format.

play.label: Google Play store icon
notes: 512x512 px, 32-bit PNG (with alpha), sRGB, at most 1024 KB.
Full square, no shadow: Google Play masks it with a radius of 30 percent of the icon size.
No badges or text that suggest ranking, price, deals or Google Play categories.

android.label: Android adaptive icon layers
notes: All layers 108x108 dp; the logo is at least 48x48 dp and at most 66x66 dp; the outer 18 dp on each side is reserved for masking and motion.
The design guide names the inner 66x66 dp as never clipped; the AdaptiveIconDrawable reference names the inner 72x72 dp as the masked viewport. The export fits the mark to the 66 dp circle.
No masks or shadows around the outline. The background layer is the plate colour as a colour resource.
The monochrome layer feeds themed icons (Android 13, API 33 and later); only its alpha is used.
Bitmaps are allowed, vectors preferred: convert favicon.svg with Android Studio's Vector Asset tool if a vector foreground is wanted.

web.label: Favicon set and PWA icons
notes: Maskable safe zone: a centred circle with a radius of 2/5 (40 percent) of the icon size; no transparent pixels in a maskable icon.
Chrome's install criteria name a 192 px and a 512 px icon. `any` and `maskable` are separate files: web.dev advises against one icon with both purposes.
Google Search: square, at least 8x8 px, larger than 48x48 px recommended; listed formats are BMP, GIF, ICO, PNG, JPEG, PPM and TIFF; one stable favicon URL per hostname.
HTML Standard: `sizes` is in raw pixels, `any` marks a scalable icon; among equally fitting icons the LAST declared wins, and /favicon.ico is the fallback when no link is declared.
favicon.ico holds PNG entries (16, 32, 48 px).

macos.label: macOS icon set
notes: AppIcon.iconset holds icon_<n>x<n>.png and icon_<n>x<n>@2x.png for 16, 32, 128, 256 and 512; 512@2x replaces a 1024 file. `iconutil -c icns` turns the folder into AppIcon.icns.
A macOS asset catalog needs an asset for each size; the same files fill it.
Current HIG: macOS shares the 1024x1024 square layout and the system masks it. An .icns file is shown as drawn on older systems, so the set is rendered with rounded corners on a transparent ground.
